slides.title: DEFINE THE BOUNDARY.
copy: Identify which components are inside or outside
slides.alt: DEFINE THE BOUNDARY. Use manufacturer-approved test locations. Identify which components are inside or outside the specified external-static boundary.

slides.title: KEEP THE SIGNS STRAIGHT.
slides.alt: KEEP THE SIGNS STRAIGHT. Illustrative return static: -0.20 in. w.g. Illustrative supply static: +0.35 in. w.g. TESP = 0.35 - (-0.20) = 0.55 in. w.g.

slides.title: A PRESSURE IS NOT A FLOW.
copy: Compare with manufacturer data for the exact
TESP alone does not establish airflow.
slides.alt: A PRESSURE IS NOT A FLOW. Compare with manufacturer data for the exact equipment and operating configuration. TESP alone does not establish airflow.

slides.title: MEASURED TESP IS NOT DESIGN ASP.
copy: Do not substitute a field pressure reading
for the available duct pressure in a design.
Use the appropriate calculation and boundary.
slides.alt: MEASURED TESP IS NOT DESIGN ASP. Do not substitute a field pressure reading for the available duct pressure in a design. Use the appropriate calculation and boundary.

slides.title: MEASURE. RECORD. THEN INTERPRET.
copy: Use the free airflow / static-pressure reference.
slides.alt: MEASURE. RECORD. THEN INTERPRET. Record conditions and test locations. Use the free airflow / static-pressure reference. AnyHVAC.net / Resources

slides.title: PRESSURE TERMS NEED A CONTEXT.
slides.alt: PRESSURE TERMS NEED A CONTEXT. Static, velocity and total pressure describe different things.

slides.title: STATIC PRESSURE.
copy: Static pressure acts in all directions.
Probe placement and flow conditions matter.
slides.alt: STATIC PRESSURE. Static pressure acts in all directions. Use an appropriate static-pressure method. Probe placement and flow conditions matter.

slides.title: VELOCITY PRESSURE.
copy: Velocity pressure relates to air motion.
Density and velocity determine its value.
It is not a substitute for a static reading.
slides.alt: VELOCITY PRESSURE. Velocity pressure relates to air motion. Density and velocity determine its value. It is not a substitute for a static reading.

slides.title: TOTAL PRESSURE.
copy: At the same point and reference basis:
slides.alt: TOTAL PRESSURE. At the same point and reference basis: total pressure = static + velocity pressure. Use compatible measurements and units.

slides.title: DROP VS EQUIPMENT TESP.
copy: TESP uses a defined equipment external boundary.
slides.alt: DROP VS EQUIPMENT TESP. Pressure drop compares specified points. TESP uses a defined equipment external boundary. These terms are not interchangeable.

slides.title: NAME THE MEASUREMENT.
copy: Define the points, basis and procedure.
slides.alt: NAME THE MEASUREMENT. Define the points, basis and procedure. Follow the manufacturer reference. AnyHVAC.net / Resources
